t_advice_summary_textbox.text: Gnomes are always in fixed pairs, certain colours lead you to a bright forest and others lead to a dark forest. Only the colours count and not the position or hat size, these factors do not matter

vb_textbox.text: Hello, I hope that you enjoy participating. I wanted to give you some advice that I learnt whilst I was playing and I hope that this helps you too.The gnomes always arrive in pairs, and they always stay within the same pairs, these are: Red and Yellow, Purple and Blue, Pink and Green, and Orange and brown. They are not always in the same position, but they always stay within their set pairs.There are two types of forest, Bright (with a red basket) and Dark (with a yellow basket), the gnomes are allocated a forest dependant on their colour, which are as follows:Bright - Red, Blue, Green and Orange. Dark - Yellow, Purple, Pink and Brown.The number of mushrooms varies each time you enter a forest.I found that sticking to one type of forest, such as bright for several rounds obtained a good amount of mushrooms, and once the number of mushrooms decreased moved onto the other forest, and vice versa. I found this allowed some sort of strategy in my selections, but remember the numbers are very variable. Good luck, and have fun, I hope you manage to collect a large amount of mushrooms!
